transcript:
Header: 2025-05-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Location: Zoom call
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maria Torres (Bluewave Head of ML), Ben Cho (Bluewave Platform Eng), Lina Park (Product)
Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming, generation params, retries, and how to run a simple POC. Maria asked about security and data retention; Ben asked about latency and retries.
Topics: hosted API, streaming, temperature/top_p, max_tokens, request retries/backoff, example SDK snippets, demo of streaming response in console
--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you. we'll do a quick 30-ish minute demo of the hosted API chat and text generation basics and then leave time for Q&A, Priya's going to demo streaming and some SDK bits.
[00:23] Maria Torres: Thanks Alex, excited - we currently do inference in-house but looking to offload some bursty workloads, main concerns are latency and data retention.
[00:37] Alex Kim: Totally, that's what we hear a lot. quick agenda: high-level hosted API, live demo (chat + streaming), params and cost tradeoffs, retries/backoff, then next steps.
[01:05] Priya Desai: I'll jump in on the demo. Quick note: our hosted API supports streaming out of the box, and you can set chunk size and partial responses. We'll show a node example, python as well in the repo link.
[01:30] Ben Cho: What does streaming mean for billing - is it per final token or per chunk?
[01:40] Priya Desai: Good q - billing is token-based on output tokens, you get the same unit billing whether you stream or not, but streaming can reduce perceived latency. Also we have payload limits per request - we'll share the docs link.
[02:05] Alex Kim: Link: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/docs/hosting/api - that'll have rate limits and tiers.
[02:22] Maria Torres: Security - do you store prompts? are they used to train models?
[02:30] Alex Kim: Short answer: no training on customer data by default for hosted - we have contractual options and you can opt out; logs for debugging are available with retention controls. we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper after.
[03:00] Priya Desai: ok demo time - opening the console, making a chat call with streaming enabled. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rw-1-large","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize our Q2 roadmap"}]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
[03:40] [demo audio/typing] Priya Desai: you'll see chunks arrive as delta tokens, client can render progressively. Here we have a small web client that appends tokens as they stream in. sometimes transcription shows KV cash but it's KV cache in the runtime.
[04:10] Lina Park: Is there an auto-retry if the stream drops mid-response?
[04:20] Priya Desai: We recommend client-side retries for idempotent requests and our SDKs have built-in reconnect helpers. For streaming we support resumable sessions in some model variants, otherwise best practice is a simple exponential backoff + idempotency key.
[04:55] Ben Cho: Latency targets - for our use case we need 95th pct under 300ms for short prompts. Can hosted achieve that?
[05:10] Alex Kim: Depends on model size and region; for small-medium models in our closest region, we can hit ~100-200ms token latency in many cases. We'll run a benchmark for you. note: Dedicated capacity gives tighter guarantees if you need hard SLOs.
[05:45] Maria Torres: How do generation params like temperature or top_p affect throughput/cost?
[05:55] Priya Desai: They don't change cost directly, cost is token-based. But lower temperature tends to produce shorter outputs which reduces tokens. Sampling params can change variance of outputs, so for deterministic outputs use temperature=0.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry, just joined - are there SDKs?
[06:30] Priya Desai: yes, node/python/go SDKs, plus curl examples. we'll drop a repo link.
[06:42] Alex Kim: We also surface token-level cost in the console so product teams can see per-route costs.
[07:10] Priya Desai: demoing python snippet: from redwood import Client; c=Client('<key>'); resp=c.chat.create(model='rw-1-large', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Write a brief email"}], stream=True) then iterate over resp.stream() to render.
[07:45] Ben Cho: Ok how about retries on 5xx - any built-in retry policy on the API gateway?
[07:55] Alex Kim: We do 3x internal retries on transient upstream errors, but recommend clients implement exponential backoff so you can handle rate limits/429s. In general, 429s should be treated as signals to back off, we return Retry-After when applicable.
[08:30] Maria Torres: Data residency - can we pin region or require EU only?
[08:40] Alex Kim: Hosted supports region pinning for enterprise tiers and we have EU regions; for strict residency you may consider Redwood Private (VPC). We'll include the private deployment brief.
[09:10] Priya Desai: Now showing the console streaming debug view where you can see tokens, token timing, and bytes. This is handy for tuning batch sizes and caching.
[09:40] Lina Park: You mentioned prefix caching - how does that work for chat?
[09:50] Priya Desai: Our runtime can KV cache repeated prefixes (we call it KV cache) and reuse cached KV to skip compute for common system prompts or repeated context, reduces cost and latency for multi-turn chats. Sometimes docs say KV cash in transcriptions, apologies.
[10:20] Ben Cho: If we do a PoC, what's a realistic scope and time?
[10:30] Alex Kim: Typical hosted POC: 1 week to integrate SDK + sample prompts, run benchmark scripts, measure latency/cost; SE helps with sample dataset and a couple of test endpoints. If you need dedicated capacity, that adds procurement time.
[11:02] Maria Torres: Are there quotas or per-key rate limits for streaming?
[11:10] Alex Kim: Yes rate limits per key; tiers documented. We'll share exact numbers in the pricing doc. Higher tiers give burst capacity.
[11:35] Priya Desai: Quick note on error modes: network drops can truncate streams - one pattern is to detect truncation and retry the full request with idempotency key, or use resumable streams for certain models.
[12:05] [12:05] Demo pause - screen-share showing sample app with streaming chat.
[15:00] Priya Desai: Switching to param tuning: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty - all supported. For text generation we often start with max_tokens=150 and temperature 0.2 for concise answers.
[16:00] Ben Cho: Do you support function/tool calling in hosted API?
[16:10] Alex Kim: Yes function calling is supported - it returns structured JSON you can parse; we can demo that in next session.
[16:30] Maria Torres: For security reviews, who signs the DPA?
[16:40] Alex Kim: We have a standard DPA, and enterprise deals can involve legal negotiation. We'll send the template.
[17:00] Priya Desai: Now live test: we run a small script to generate responses and stream them back to the client - showing latency numbers in the console. average token latency ~120ms in this region for this model.
[18:10] Lina Park: If we have bursty traffic, will you throttle?
[18:20] Alex Kim: For hosted we have rate limits per key, plus autoscaling in the backend; for predictable high-throughput you might choose Dedicated. We can also set burst allowances on higher tiers.
[19:00] Ben Cho: About cost optimization - any recommendations?
[19:10] Priya Desai: Use prefix caching, set sensible max_tokens, consider quantized smaller models for non-critical tasks, batch requests when possible and use streaming to improve UX without significantly changing cost. Redwood Optimize can provide model recommendations based on workload.
[20:00] Maria Torres: Can we run your benchmark against our sample to validate latency?
[20:10] Alex Kim: Absolutely - Priya will share the benchmark script. If you want, we can run it from your region or have you run it and share results.
[21:00] [21:00] Short pause for checking links.
[22:15] Priya Desai: Covering retries in more detail: implement exponential backoff, idempotency keys for non-streaming calls; for streaming detect truncation and either retry or fallback to non-streaming. We'll include example psuedo-code in the repo.
[23:05] Maria Torres: Any known limits with long contexts?
[23:15] Priya Desai: Models have context windows; we offer model variants with larger windows. Also runtime-level KV cache helps with repeated system prompts. For very long contexts, consider summarization or retrieval-augmented generation.
[24:40] Ben Cho: Integration hooks - do you provide webhooks for async completions?
[24:50] Alex Kim: Yes async endpoints and webhooks supported for background jobs. We'll add the webhook docs link.
[25:30] Lina Park: What's the onboarding like for a product team - keys, SSO, RBAC?
[25:40] Alex Kim: Self-serve keys, enterprise SSO/SAML, role-based access in console, and audit logs for admin. Private deployments add KMS/HSM options.
[26:20] Priya Desai: Demo wrap-up - showed streaming, params, retries, console debug.
[26:40] Maria Torres: Great - could you also show how to measure per-request cost in the console?
[26:50] Alex Kim: Yes, console has per-route cost breakdown; we can give a guided tour in the next call.
[27:20] Ben Cho: For POC we'd want a small SLA window and guaranteed region. Is that possible for hosted?
[27:30] Alex Kim: For short POCs we can provide regional pinning for enterprise trial accounts; full SLA-backed guarantees come with Dedicated.
[28:00] Maria Torres: Any native observability integrations?
[28:10] Priya Desai: We have tracing hooks and can export logs to your logging stack via S3 or partner integrations.
[29:00] [29:00] Quick lightning questions from Lina: can we limit model choices per team?
[29:10] Alex Kim: Yes RBAC + per-route model pinning in console.
[29:40] Maria Torres: Ok recap and next steps?
[29:50] Alex Kim: Recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 doc, Priya will send benchmark scripts and streaming example repo, Ben to share sample dataset and latency goals, schedule POC kickoff for 2025-05-20.
[30:20] Maria Torres: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[30:30] Ben Cho: Thanks, that was helpful.
[30:40] Priya Desai: I'll follow up with the links in the CRM note and slack.
[32:00] [End of meeting - call closed]
